title: Money must only be formatted through lib/invoices
body:
Amounts are integer cents. Pages and components must format them with `formatAmount` or `formatCurrency` from `lib/invoices.ts`, never inline (`amountCents / 100`, `.toFixed(2)`, a new `Intl.NumberFormat`). An inline format rounds differently and drifts from the CSV export. Nothing stops a change from doing it today; make that a check that fails.

---

spec.plan: Before: nothing stops a page or component from formatting integer cents inline (`amountCents / 100`, `.toFixed(...)`, `new Intl.NumberFormat`), which rounds differently from the CSV export; `npm run lint` passes on such code. After: `eslint.config.mjs` gains one config object scoped to `files: ["app/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "components/**/*.{ts,tsx}"]` with `ignores: ["**/*.test.{ts,tsx}"]`, appended as the last argument of the existing `tseslint.config(...)` call, that sets `"no-restricted-syntax": ["error", ...]` with exactly three entries, each `{ selector, message }` sharing one message string held in a `const` above the export: (1) `BinaryExpression[operator='/'][right.type='Literal'][right.value=100]`, (2) `CallExpression[callee.property.name='toFixed']`, (3) `MemberExpression[object.name='Intl'][property.name='NumberFormat']` (this catches `new Intl.NumberFormat(...)`, `Intl.NumberFormat(...)` and aliasing it). The message must read: "Amounts are integer cents: format them with formatAmount or formatCurrency from @/lib/invoices, so the page rounds the same way the CSV export does." Add a one-line why-comment above the block, matching the file's comment style. `lib/` is out of scope on purpose because `lib/invoices.ts` is where `formatAmount`/`formatCurrency` legitimately do this. Test files are exempt because the request names pages and components, and tests assert literal strings. No existing rule, ignore or setting in `eslint.config.mjs` changes, so this tightens the guardrail and does not loosen it. The repo has zero existing violations (verified), so there is nothing to fix and nothing to baseline; leave `.factory/guardrails/baselines.json` untouched. To prove the rule, add a new root test file `lint-rules.test.ts`. Its first line is `// @vitest-environment node`. It builds one `new ESLint()` from `eslint` (the repo's own config, cwd = repo root) and uses `lintText(code, { filePath })` with virtual paths, counting messages whose `ruleId === "no-restricted-syntax"`. Name it `lint-rules.test.ts`, not `eslint.config.test.ts`, because policy's guardrail glob `eslint.config.*` would match the latter. No application file changes. In the PR body, state the rule in plain words, show the bad example failing and the good one passing, and say 0 existing violations.
acceptance_checks: On the built tree, `npm run lint` exits 0 with no output: the new rule finds no existing violation, including in lib/invoices.ts, which still uses `/ 100`, `.toFixed(2)` and `new Intl.NumberFormat`.

Replace `{formatAmount(i.amountCents)}` in app/invoices/page.tsx with `{(i.amountCents / 100).toFixed(2)}` and run `npm run lint`: it exits non-zero, reports two `no-restricted-syntax` errors on that line, and the message names formatAmount and formatCurrency. Revert the edit.

Add `const fmt = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD" });` inside the component in components/ExportButton.tsx and run `npm run lint`: it exits non-zero with a `no-restricted-syntax` error on that line. Revert the edit.
Add the same `(c / 100).toFixed(2)` expression to a function in lib/invoices.ts and run `npm run lint`: it exits 0, because lib is where formatting belongs. Revert the edit.
`npm test` passes, and its output includes lint-rules.test.ts with every test in it passing.

Start the app and open http://localhost:3000/invoices: the page still shows the five invoices, amounts such as 245.00 and 1180.00, 'Total sent: $1,497.50', and the button 'Export 3 invoices as CSV', unchanged from before.
tests_added: lint-rules.test.ts: a page (filePath app/invoices/page.tsx) that renders `(amountCents / 100).toFixed(2)` fails the money-formatting rule, so an amount that rounds differently from the CSV cannot land on a page
lint-rules.test.ts: a component (filePath components/Example.tsx) that builds its own `new Intl.NumberFormat(...)` fails the rule
lint-rules.test.ts: the same page using `formatAmount` and `formatCurrency` imported from `@/lib/invoices` passes with zero `no-restricted-syntax` messages
lint-rules.test.ts: the inline expression in lib/invoices.ts (filePath lib/invoices.ts) is allowed, because that is where the formatting is supposed to live

research.claim: formatAmount and formatCurrency are the two formatters in lib/invoices.ts. They are themselves built from `/ 100`, `.toFixed(2)` and `new Intl.NumberFormat`, so the rule must exclude lib/ and target only app/ and components/.
The CSV export formats amounts through formatAmount, so an inline format on a page can drift from the export.
The /invoices page already formats only through formatAmount and formatCurrency, so there are no existing violations to fix or baseline.
